preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership through social engineering/compromise)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the mint() function to create new tokens for your own address, effectively printing unlimited tokens and diluting the value for all other holders. Alternatively, set the FeeAddress to your own address and manipulate txFee/burnFee to extract value from every transaction, or blacklist other users to freeze their funds.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CoinToken contract has owner-only privileged functions. The owner can call mint() to create unlimited tokens for any address, effectively printing money and diluting other holders' value. This is a classic owner privilege abuse vulnerability where the contract owner has unlimited minting authority.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call the mint() function to mint a large amount of tokens to our address, increasing our balance.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Get the current owner address from the contract
2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner
3. Call mint(attacker, 1_000_000 * 10^decimals) to mint tokens
4. Stop impersonation
5. Verify our balance increased
